# Three actual caps force source-parity vacancy in every continuous dimension at least four

This extends the audited d=4 calculation in `candidate ac5edf6664902ea2`. The proof is uniform in d>=4, but remains a specific n=1 simplex mechanism. It is not a proof of OC or of a general capacity-to-parity inequality.

## Statement

Let d>=4, let T be a d-simplex of volume V and barycentrics lambda_0,...,lambda_d, and let

    D_delta={x in T: sum_{i=2}^d lambda_i(x)<=delta},
    0<delta<1/(d+1).

Let an actual convex body have fibers K_-1=D_delta and K_0=T. Assume its nonempty sampled fibers have positive d-volume. In its pure outward-smoothed problem, with the actual pooled within-fiber covariance norm, suppose base zero has a deepest mark Y_0 with proper own core. Suppose three ACTUAL active caps, indexed 2,3,4, have scaled margins

    a_i z+f_i(x),  f_i(y_0)=0,
    sup_T |f_i−(lambda_i−1/(d+1))| <=1/[20(d+1)],

miss D_delta completely and have zero transition-strip coarea on all other fibers. If 0<h<1/(1000d), base zero is the only deepest integer base.

The cap scaling is positive and rescales its covariance width as well, leaving its actual smoothed integrand unchanged. The proof uses the established strict exclusion of another deepest mark, not an assumed rounding of a centroid.

## 1. Convexity and possible source bases

Every barycentric coordinate has minimum zero on both D_delta and T. Convexity of the fiber minimum therefore puts every fiber at real base t>=0 inside T. For R=sum_{i=2}^d lambda_i, the minimum is zero on both fibers and the maxima are delta and one. If a fiber at −2 existed, the convex minimum would be nonnegative there while the concave maximum would be at most 2delta−1<0. Hence no integer base below −1 exists.

The left fiber volume is

    |D_delta|/V=d delta^(d−1)−(d−1)delta^d
               <d/5^(d−1)<=4/125.

The first identity is the elementary Beta(d−1,2) integral. The final sequence decreases for integer d>=4. Since the simplex centroid already supplies raw depth Gamma_d V and Gamma_d>=1/e>4/11, the exposed base −1 cannot be deepest.

Any other deepest integer base must be adjacent to zero: otherwise the smooth deepest-set convexity and full-normal identity would force an integer interpolation of distinct deepest marks. Consequently a second source would have to occur at base one.

## 2. A second source would force three small coordinate maxima

Assume base one is deepest. Strict actual-source exclusion and zero outside coarea force each of the three selected cap integrands to vanish on the WHOLE K_1. Write w_i=h Gamma(grad f_i)>0. Complete misses at bases −1 and one imply

    max_D f_i−a_i<=−w_i,
    max_K1 f_i+a_i<=−w_i.

The vertex e_0 lies in D_delta. Put eta=1/[20(d+1)]. Since f_i(e_0)>=−1/(d+1)−eta, and K_1 lies in T, these inequalities give

    lambda_i(x)<=2/(d+1)+2eta=21/[10(d+1)]=:b,
    x in K_1, i=2,3,4.                              (1)

For d>=4, b<=21/50<1/2. The concave maximum of lambda_2 at base two would therefore be at most 2b−1<0, contradicting its nonnegative minimum. Thus base one is exposed among all integer fibers.

## 3. A dimension-uniform volume deficit

Inclusion-exclusion for the three events lambda_i>b, dropping the nonnegative triple-intersection subtraction, gives

    |K_1|/V <= 1−3A_d+3B_d,
    A_d=(1−b)^d,
    B_d=(1−2b)^d.                                   (2)

We use deliberately conservative rational estimates. For any c>=2 and real x+1>c, the function

    F_c(x)=(1−c/(x+1))^x

is increasing. To verify this, set t=1/(x+1). Its logarithmic derivative is

    log(1−ct)+ct(1−t)/(1−ct)
      =sum_{k>=2} c^(k−1)[c(1−1/k)−1]t^k >=0.

The series converges because ct<1, and every coefficient is nonnegative. With c=21/10 and x>=4, this gives

    A_d >=(29/50)^4.

Also b>=2/(d+1), so

    B_d <=(1−4/(d+1))^d < e^(−4)<1/50.

For the middle inequality use log(1−s)<=−s−s²/2 with s=4/(d+1), giving an exponent at most

    −4d/(d+1)−8d/(d+1)^2 <−4.

The last inequality follows from e>8/3 and (8/3)^4>50. Thus (2) gives the exact bound

    |K_1|/V <=1−3(29/50)^4+3/50
             =4503157/6250000 <8/11.                (3)

The elementary series bound e<11/4 gives Gamma_d>=1/e>4/11. Hence the right side of (3) is strictly below 2Gamma_d, uniformly in d.

## 4. Smooth exposed-fiber depth also has a strict deficit

At any mark of K_1, take the two opposite continuous normals grad lambda_2. Their smoothed own masses sum to at most

    |K_1|+|T intersect {|lambda_2−lambda_2(y)|<=w}|,
    w=h Gamma(grad lambda_2).

Every remaining fiber is inside T, so its lambda_2 variance is at most 1/4. The actual pooled within-fiber covariance therefore gives w<=h/2. The lambda_2 marginal of uniform T is d(1−s)^(d−1)V, bounded by dV. The slab in the last display has volume at most 2dwV<=dhV. At least one own cap consequently has mass at most

    |K_1|/2+dhV/2
       <[4503157/12500000+1/2000]V
       <(4/11)V <Gamma_d V.                         (4)

The rational middle comparison is strict; indeed
4/11−4503157/12500000=465273/137500000>1/2000.
Because base one is exposed, a finite sufficiently large base tilt isolates either selected own cap from every other fiber. Thus (4) bounds actual mixed smooth depth at every point of K_1. It contradicts the raw lower bound Gamma_d V supplied by the middle simplex centroid.

No second deepest base exists, as claimed.

## Scope

The three-cap hypothesis is concrete and testable on the actual active family. It is satisfied by the certified small-parameter thin-edge obstruction when d=4. The calculation shows that its geometric source-vacancy mechanism extends in continuous dimension, without asserting a corresponding all-dimensional capacity obstruction or a general n-dimensional allocation principle. In higher integer dimension, an endpoint exposed along one integer line need not be globally exposed; that distinction prevents simply applying this statement along every midpoint-forest edge.
